_readme: NEUTRAL TEMPLATE — works for any language / framework / domain, frontend OR backend. Copy this, then fill in YOUR project's canon surfaces. Two worked examples ship alongside: stack.config.example.backend.json and stack.config.example.frontend.json. Nothing here assumes a web app; the frontend block is OFF by default. The gates only govern what you declare — an empty block is an inert gate.

machinery._readme: The DISCOVER-THEN-REUSE anti-hand-roll detectors. Declare YOUR codebase's hand-roll shapes so the gates force reuse of what already exists. signals[] = [{re, name}] code shapes that reproduce an existing helper; builderRe = a body-fragment matching a new reusable builder that must be exported not private; reusableExportRe reserved. ALL EMPTY = these gates do nothing.

frontend._readme: OPT-IN CSS/DOM module. enabled:false => no frontend-specific detector runs. Backend projects leave this off. See frontend/README.md.

verification._readme: TWO halves. (1) the scripted-API-only gate: a call on a browserTool is denied unless it invokes an allowedCalls function. (2) instruments[]: the roster of things allowed to VOUCH for a run. A run writes a RECEIPT; the receipt names its instrument; a receipt naming an instrument nobody declared is REFUSED (fail closed). ONE receipt shape serves every instrument — a browser driver and a desktop driver differ only in where a frame comes from, never in what a receipt says. An entry with enabled:false is declared but inert and its receipts are refused. Read the reader with: node hooks/verification-first.js --receipt <path>

specCatalog._readme: CONSTRAINT-BEFORE instead of refusal-AFTER (integrations/spec-catalog.md). The code registry is projected into a catalog + a byte-capped prompt; a builder emits a {helper, props, children} spec that can only name catalog entries; compile.js emits real calls + an HMAC receipt; hooks/spec-gate.js refuses a new surface no receipt covers. enabled:false => every piece of this is inert.
